name: Slack
description: Let your AI work in Slack: find channels and people, read channel history and threads, catch up on what was said, post messages and thread replies, and react with emoji. One workspace, through a Slack app you install yourself.
instructions:
## Slack
This connector works in one Slack workspace through the **Slack Web API** (`https://slack.com/api`): list channels and people, read channel history and threads, post messages and replies, and add reactions. It authenticates with a token from a Slack app that you create and install in your own workspace (about 5 minutes).

**Setup**
1. Open https://api.slack.com/apps → **Create New App** → **From a manifest** → pick the workspace.
2. Paste this manifest (JSON) and click **Create**:
```json
{
  "display_information": {
    "name": "AnythingMCP"
  },
  "features": {
    "bot_user": {
      "display_name": "AnythingMCP",
      "always_online": false
    }
  },
  "oauth_config": {
    "scopes": {
      "bot": [
        "channels:read",
        "channels:history",
        "channels:join",
        "groups:read",
        "groups:history",
        "im:read",
        "im:history",
        "mpim:read",
        "mpim:history",
        "chat:write",
        "reactions:write",
        "users:read"
      ]
    }
  },
  "settings": {
    "org_deploy_enabled": false,
    "socket_mode_enabled": false,
    "token_rotation_enabled": false
  }
}
```
3. **Install App → Install to Workspace** and allow. If the workspace only lets admins install apps, Slack sends an approval request to a workspace admin instead.
4. **OAuth & Permissions → Bot User OAuth Token** (starts with `xoxb-`): paste it into `SLACK_TOKEN` and install the connector.
5. Keep **token rotation** off (as in the manifest): with rotation on, the token expires every 12 hours and a pasted token stops working.

**Bot token or user token**
- A **bot token** (`xoxb-`, the default) acts as the app: messages are posted by "AnythingMCP", and it reads the history of a channel only once the app is a member. Public channels: `slack_join_channel`, or `/invite @AnythingMCP` in the channel. Private channels, group DMs: invite the app with `/invite @AnythingMCP`.
- A **user token** (`xoxp-`) acts as the person who installed the app: it sees every conversation that person sees and posts in their name. To get one, add the same scopes plus `search:read` under `oauth_config.scopes.user` in the manifest (App Manifest page), reinstall, and paste the **User OAuth Token** instead. Only a user token can search, so `slack_search_messages` is installed switched off: turn it on when you use a user token.
- Add `users:read.email` to the scopes if the AI should see people's email addresses.

**Conversations and ids**: every call takes ids, not names: channel ids start with `C` (public), `G` (some private), `D` (direct messages); user ids with `U` or `W`. Look them up with `slack_list_conversations` and `slack_list_users`. `types` chooses what is listed: `public_channel` (default), `private_channel`, `mpim` (group DMs), `im` (direct messages), comma-separated.

**Messages, threads and timestamps**: a message is identified by its channel and its `ts` (e.g. `1712345678.123456`), which is also its time in Unix seconds. A reply to a thread has `thread_ts` set to the parent's `ts`; `slack_get_thread_replies` with the parent's `ts` returns the parent followed by the replies, and `slack_post_message` with `thread_ts` replies in the thread. `oldest` and `latest` bound the history in Unix seconds. Messages use Slack mrkdwn (`*bold*`, `_italic_`, `<https://example.com|link text>`, `<@U123>` to mention someone); `text` should stay under 4,000 characters.

**Pagination**: lists return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; pass it as `cursor` with the same other arguments while it is not empty. `has_more` says whether more history exists. Search pages with `page` (see `messages.paging`).

**Rate limits**: per method and per workspace. `conversations.list` and `users.list` allow about 20 calls a minute, `conversations.history` and `conversations.replies` about 50 a minute for an app installed in your own workspace, `chat.postMessage` about one message per second per channel. Over a limit Slack answers HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

**Errors**: Slack answers HTTP 200 with `"ok": false` and an `error` code; the connector reports these as errors.
- `invalid_auth`, `not_authed`, `token_revoked`, `token_expired`, `account_inactive`: the token is wrong, was revoked, or the app was uninstalled. Paste a fresh token.
- `missing_scope` (the `needed` field names the scope): add the scope to the app, reinstall it, and paste the new token if it changed.
- `not_in_channel`: the app is not a member of the channel; join it or invite the app.
- `channel_not_found`: a wrong id, or a private conversation the token cannot see.
- `not_allowed_token_type`: the method needs the other kind of token (search needs a user token).
- `is_archived`, `msg_too_long`, `no_text`, `already_reacted`, `invalid_name` (emoji names go without colons): fix the input.

**Out of scope here**: editing or deleting messages, files, channel management beyond joining, user groups, Slack Connect administration and Enterprise Grid org-wide installs.

SLACK_TOKEN.label: Slack token
SLACK_TOKEN.help: api.slack.com/apps → your app → OAuth & Permissions: the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…), or the User OAuth Token (xoxp-…) to act as yourself and search.
SLACK_TOKEN.patternMessage: Paste the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…) or the User OAuth Token (xoxp-…), without the word Bearer.

verifyHints.401: Slack refused the token (invalid_auth or token_revoked). Copy it again from OAuth & Permissions in your Slack app; if the app was reinstalled or uninstalled, the old token no longer works.
verifyHints.403: The token lacks a scope this call needs, or the app is not in the channel. Add the scope in the app settings and reinstall, or invite the app to the channel.
verifyHints.rate_limited: Slack is rate limiting this method. Wait for the Retry-After time and try again.

prerequisites: A Slack app created from the manifest below and installed in your workspace (about 5 minutes). Workspaces that restrict app installs need a workspace admin to approve it.

tools.name: slack_auth_test
tools.description: Check the token and return who it acts as: workspace name, URL and id, the user id, and for a bot token the bot id.

tools.name: slack_list_conversations
tools.description: List the workspace's conversations the token can see: public channels by default, and private channels, group DMs or direct messages on request. Returns id, name, topic, purpose, archive and membership state per conversation, plus next_cursor for the next page.

types.description: Comma-separated conversation types: public_channel (default), private_channel, mpim, im, e.g. "public_channel,private_channel".

exclude_archived.description: true to leave out archived channels (default false).

cursor.description: response_metadata.next_cursor from the previous response, to fetch the next page with the same other arguments.

team_id.description: Workspace id; only needed with a token of an org-wide Enterprise Grid app.

tools.name: slack_get_conversation_info
tools.description: Get the details of one channel or conversation by id: name, topic, purpose, creator, creation time, archive state and whether the token is a member, optionally with the member count.

tools.name: slack_get_conversation_history
tools.description: Read the messages of a channel or conversation, newest first, optionally within a time window. Each message has its ts, user, text, thread_ts and reply count when it starts a thread, and reactions; has_more and next_cursor page further back.

oldest.description: Only messages after this Unix timestamp in seconds, e.g. "1759276800" or a message ts.

latest.description: Only messages before this Unix timestamp in seconds (default now).

inclusive.description: true to include messages exactly at oldest or latest.

cursor.description: response_metadata.next_cursor from the previous response, to fetch the next page with the same other arguments.

tools.name: slack_get_thread_replies
tools.description: Read a thread: the parent message followed by its replies in order, for a channel and the parent message's ts. has_more and next_cursor page through long threads.

channel.description: Conversation id the thread is in.

ts.description: ts of the thread's parent message (its thread_ts), e.g. "1712345678.123456".

oldest.description: Only replies after this Unix timestamp in seconds.

latest.description: Only replies before this Unix timestamp in seconds.

inclusive.description: true to include replies exactly at oldest or latest.

cursor.description: response_metadata.next_cursor from the previous response, to fetch the next page with the same other arguments.

tools.name: slack_list_users
tools.description: List the members of the workspace, including bots, invited and deactivated accounts, with id, name, real name, display name, title, time zone and flags such as deleted, is_bot and is_admin. Email addresses appear only with the users:read.email scope.

limit.description: Maximum users per page, 1 to 1000 (Slack recommends 200 or fewer for large workspaces).

cursor.description: response_metadata.next_cursor from the previous response, to fetch the next page with the same other arguments.

team_id.description: Workspace id; only needed with a token of an org-wide Enterprise Grid app.

tools.name: slack_get_user_info
tools.description: Get one person's profile by user id: name, real and display name, title, time zone, status, and whether the account is deleted, a bot or an admin. The email address appears only with the users:read.email scope.

tools.name: slack_join_channel
tools.description: Make the app a member of a public channel so it can read the channel's history. Private channels cannot be joined this way: someone in the channel invites the app instead.

channel.description: Id of the public channel, e.g. C0123456789.

tools.name: slack_post_message
tools.description: Post a message to a channel or conversation, or as a reply in a thread when thread_ts is given. Returns the posted message with its ts and the channel id.

channel.description: Conversation id to post in, e.g. C0123456789.

text.description: Message text in Slack mrkdwn, up to 4,000 characters.

thread_ts.description: ts of the parent message to reply in its thread.

reply_broadcast.description: With thread_ts: true to also show the reply in the channel (default false).

unfurl_links.description: false to stop link previews for text links.

unfurl_media.description: false to stop previews of media links.

tools.name: slack_add_reaction
tools.description: Add an emoji reaction to a message, identified by its channel and ts.

name.description: Emoji name without colons, e.g. "thumbsup", "white_check_mark" or "thumbsup::skin-tone-3".

tools.name: slack_search_messages
tools.description: Search messages across the workspace with Slack search syntax (in:#channel, from:@name, before:, after:, has:link). Works only with a user token (xoxp-) that has the search:read scope. Returns matches with channel, user, ts, text and permalink, and paging information.

sort.description: Sort by relevance (score, default) or time (timestamp).
